Khtanga, Artic Siberia 
Because the polar winter brings long periods of darkness and low visibility, these stilt houses are often painted in vibrant colors (blues, yellows, reds) to combat visual monotony and seasonal depression.

■The fact the ground consists of soil and ice cemented together, conventional foundations cannot be used. If a heated building sits directly on the tundra, its warmth seeps downward, melts the underground ice, and turns the foundation into unstable mud, causing the structure to crack, tilt, or entirely collapse.

■Deep-Driven Piles: 
Reinforced concrete or steel piles are driven deep into the continuous permafrost layer, past the unstable topsoil ("active layer") that naturally thaws and freezes each summer.

■The Cold Air Gap: 
Buildings are intentionally elevated 5 to 10 feet off the ground. This empty space allows sub-zero Arctic winds to circulate freely beneath the floorboards all year. The freezing air keeps the underlying permafrost frozen and structurally stable, absorbing any radiant heat escaping the building.
